title: Staged telemetry & degraded-mode upgrade acceptance for zero‑egress VPC deployments
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: PRD: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for performing software upgrades and maintaining operational telemetry for Private/VPC deployments that operate with zero or minimal egress. The goal is to allow operator-led upgrades (canary, staged), safety-tested offline fallbacks, and degraded-mode telemetry that preserves enough observability for safe rollouts without requiring unrestricted outbound network access. This document clarifies networking constraints, artifact distribution approaches for air-gapped sites, required runtime telemetry, and concrete acceptance tests for upgrades and rollbacks.
scope: IN-SCOPE: (1) Acceptance criteria for upgrades where clusters have no outbound egress except to approved mirrors or proxies; (2) Telemetry surfaces required during upgrades (health, KV cache hit rates, kernel errors, token-level cost deltas); (3) Staged canary & site-by-site upgrade sequencing with operator APIs and CLI tools; (4) Offline artifact distribution using signed bundles and mirror validation. OUT-OF-SCOPE: (1) Full redesign of the operator; (2) New commercial licensing flows; (3) Hardware provisioning or physical media logistics beyond spec and verification checks.
requirements: R1: Upgrade artifacts must be signed and verifiable locally (SHA256 + signature) with stated provenance metadata.

R2: Cluster bootstrap and upgrade must support an approved mirror endpoint or local mirror (HTTP/HTTPS) with optional TLS client certs; fallback to physical-media install must be supported and testable.
R3: Telemetry to be emitted even in degraded networks: node health (CPU/GPU), runtime errors, batching latency, KV cache miss rate, per-model token latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99).
R4: During upgrades, the operator must provide a dry-run mode that validates artifact checksums, manifest compatibility, and rollback artifacts without applying changes to production pods.
R5: Canary policy must allow rolling upgrades across N sites with configurable blast radius and automatic halt on thresholded metrics (error rate > 2% or p99 latency regression > 30%).
R6: System must be able to validate and apply incremental patches in offline (air-gapped) environments without temporary full egress by using staged mirrors or signed bundles.
R7: Upgrade plan must expose an operator-visible preflight checklist and an automated verification step that verifies basic inference throughput and correctness on a small prompt set post-upgrade.
R8: Audit logs for upgrade actions must be exportable to customer-provided SIEMs; in zero-egress mode, audit export may be to local storage or pulled via approved mirror synchronization.
R9: Registry compatibility: we must support image manifests from internal registries and allow image provenance pinning in the cluster config.
R10: Time synchronization guidance: NTP/PTP requirements and offline clock drift mitigation steps must be documented and verifiable during preflight.
R11: Split-horizon DNS and egress exception guidance must be provided to customers, including a validation tool that simulates blocked egress and reports missing endpoints.
R12: Security: all upgrade flows must preserve KMS/HSM key custody; key rotation during upgrades must be supported with a documented sequence and rollback plan.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A test zero-egress cluster can perform a full upgrade from vX.Y to vX.Y+1 using only a configured internal mirror endpoint; artifacts verified by signature and checksum.

AC-2: During a staged canary rollout on a 3-site test topology, automated halting triggers if any site exceeds error or latency thresholds; operator receives clear actionable reason and remediation steps.

AC-3: Telemetry surface area (node health, batch latency, KV cache hit/miss, model token latency p50/p95/p99) is available via the Console and via a local Prometheus endpoint even when external metrics ingestion is blocked.
AC-4: Dry-run upgrade completes and produces a deterministic verification report (compatibility checks, manifest diffs, expected rollout duration) without mutating cluster state.

AC-5: Offline bundle installation path documented and exercised: at least one team member performs a manual install using a signed bundle and validates post-install correctness against the canonical prompt set.
AC-6: Audit logs for upgrade actions are written locally and can be pulled to a customer SIEM; sample export script exists and has been run successfully in test environment.
AC-7: The split-horizon DNS / egress validation tool reports zero unresolved endpoints and a passable guidance report for customers to remediate network policies.
AC-8: Security review sign-off obtained and KMS key custody verification documented and validated in a non-production private deployment.

AC-9: Automated rollback plan succeeds in returning to pre-upgrade state within SLO-defined window (operator-observed rollback completes within 15 minutes for control-plane-only regression scenarios).
test_plan: T1: Create three test clusters with varying egress: (a) full egress, (b) mirror-only, (c) zero-egress with physical bundle install. Run same upgrade path and record success/failure and times.
T2: Execute dry-run mode against each cluster; validate produced verification report against expected manifest deltas and dependency lists.
T3: Run canary workload generator during staged rollout to verify threshold triggers; intentionally inject a regression on canary site to ensure automatic halt and alerting.
T4: Validate telemetry endpoints by disabling external metrics ingestion and confirming Console and local Prometheus show required metrics with correct labels and cardinality.
T5: Perform manual signed-bundle offline install and run the post-upgrade canonical prompt test suite to verify inference correctness and cost delta metrics.
T6: Simulate KMS rotation during upgrade and verify operator sequence, key fallback, and ability to rollback if rotations fail.
T7: Run integration test that pulls audit logs and ingests into a test SIEM instance; verify log completeness and timestamp ordering.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Staging validation — deploy to internal lab clusters with mirror-only egress; run T1-T4.
Phase 1: Beta customer pilots — invite 2 pilot customers on Dedicated/Private to opt into staged telemetry and perform supervised upgrades.
Phase 2: Operator tooling release — ship CLI flags (dry-run, mirror-only mode, signed-bundle apply) and the split-horizon validator tool to GA.
Phase 3: Wide availability — after successful pilots and security sign-off, include as default upgrade option for private deployments in private-2026.04 release.
Communications: Provide step-by-step runbooks, required customer network checklists, and a knowledge base article for offline installs.
monitoring_and_alerting: M1: Primary metrics: control-plane upgrade progress, canary inference error rate, model token latency p99, KV cache miss rate, batching latency p95.

M2: Alerts: upgrade-halt (error rate > 2% sustained 5m), telemetry-loss (no telemetry for 10m), audit-rotation-failure (failed to write audit to local store), mirror-unreachable (mirror endpoint connection failure).
M3: Dashboard: a dedicated upgrade-run dashboard showing preflight results, artifact provenance, per-site health and a visible rollback button for operators.
M4: Burn rate: track token cost delta during canary vs baseline to detect unexpected cost regression.
rollback_plan: If post-deploy verification fails or thresholds are exceeded, the operator can trigger an automated rollback that uses pre-created rollback artifacts. Rollback must validate cluster state and re-run post-rollback verification. For air-gapped installs, rollback artifacts must be present on the mirror or local bundle before starting the upgrade; if missing, upgrade must be halted and the operator instructed to stage rollback bundle via provided checklist.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoffs: preserving telemetry in zero-egress mode requires additional local storage and longer retention for batch logs; we accept higher local disk usage to avoid enabling egress. There's a small increase in release engineering complexity to maintain signed bundles and regression test suites. We prioritize safety and auditability over speed for air-gapped flows. Long-term we may automate mirror synchronization but initial scope focuses on operator-driven processes.
open_questions: Q1: Do we require customer-supplied TLS client certs for mirror auth by default, or support token-based mirror auth as an option?
Q2: What is the maximum acceptable local storage footprint for retained telemetry logs in zero-egress clusters?
Q3: Should rollback artifacts be produced automatically by CI for every release, or only for LTS and major patch releases?
Q4: Who is the final approver for air-gapped security sign-off (Security team contact)?
